scoring.heatBonus: 0-2 points after the 10-point base rubric; final score capped at 10; primary verification and base editorial score >= 6.0 are mandatory

hardRules: Use at least one primary source whenever one is publicly available. For Market / Business stories with no public primary document, a narrow exception allows high-quality financial reporting when the reported/negotiating status is stated explicitly and corroboration meets the Market / Business evidence rule.
Use the original announcement or release time for recency.
Do not cover a story already present in history or the current story file.

Do not publish rumours, unconfirmed leaks, predictions presented as fact, or unverified benchmark claims. Confirmed data/credential leaks and verified breach incidents are valid cybersecurity stories.

The core of every story must be a meaningful technical/scientific development, mathematical or research result, cybersecurity incident/finding, product/capability release, hardware/robotics/infrastructure change, meaningful open-source release, or a material market/business development involving AI companies, Big Tech, or major consulting firms.

Exclude hiring/recruitment, fellowships, training cohorts, trivial staffing news, routine partnerships, small/routine funding announcements, ordinary customer wins, and generic company expansion unless there is a material technical, strategic, cybersecurity, or market/business consequence.
Write narration first, then split that exact narration into short voice-first beats.
Beat text must reproduce narration exactly and in order.
Do not manually time visual beats; timing comes from narration word boundaries.
Prefer source imagery, screenshots, metrics, symbols, diagrams, comparisons and memes over explanatory on-screen copy.
Do not put paragraphs on screen.
When using company-reported benchmarks, explicitly attribute them in narration.
Use memes as editorial punctuation, not random filler.
Use full-screen cutaways for standalone visual punchlines; cutaways pause narration and hide captions automatically.
Short visual meme cutaways must play to a natural end; reject long cutaway videos instead of hard-trimming them.
Silent meme images and silent meme videos must never appear as standalone full-screen cutaways; composite them alongside the main visual instead.
Use at least four visual treatment families and avoid repeating the same composition across consecutive beats.
Editorial reaction-cue phrases such as 'the headline sounds wild' should be considered meme opportunities.
Do not cut visuals on every narration fragment; the renderer should group semantic beats into readable visual windows.
Short sound effects and meme-audio reactions must play to their natural end rather than being clipped to the current narration beat.
When useful official imagery exists, reuse multiple distinct source images across the Short instead of replacing everything with diagrams.
Meme overlays should float directly over the main visual without a default card, border, or framed box.
Narration must read like spoken editorial copy with a hook, concrete technical explanation, a limitation/catch, and a concise implication or punchline when appropriate.
Source images must semantically match the beat query; reject low-confidence images rather than forcing them into the edit.
Explanatory animations should visualize transformation, capacity, causality, hierarchy, or movement rather than restating narration as labels.
Do not automatically assign reaction memes to structural transition phrases such as 'here is the catch'.
Do not let page-global metadata make unrelated source images appear semantically relevant.
Do not collapse distinct adjacent explanatory animations merely to maximize treatment-family diversity.
Source visuals about a named product, game, model, person, or feature must require identifying asset-local terms via mustMatch.
Do not reuse the same source image for unrelated beats unless reuse is explicitly justified.
Explanatory animations must not occupy consecutive visual windows when a valid source, logo, comparison, chart, timeline, metric, or other treatment is available.
Keep explanatory-animation windows to roughly one third of the finished Short; variety is more important than maximizing diagram usage.
Use Kokoro-82M as the primary narration path; Edge neural voices are fallback only, with no artificial pitch shifting or heavy compression.
Treat explain, charts, timelines, comparisons, flows, diagrams and networks as one abstract-tech family; together they should occupy no more than roughly one third of final visual windows.
Never show two abstract-tech visual windows consecutively; use source imagery, branding, memes, metrics, text/symbol moments or kinetic typography as a visual reset.
Use Kokoro-82M as the primary narration engine; Edge neural voices are fallback only.
Write humor into the narration itself using dry observations, analogies, reactions, punchlines and callbacks; memes amplify written beats rather than rescue dry copy.
Prefer real/source media over standalone branding whenever a semantically valid source asset exists.
Standalone logo windows are rare, never consecutive, and capped at two in a normal 25-40 second Short.
Source imagery must preserve meaningful edge content; landscape media should be contained over an aspect-aware blurred/darkened background instead of destructively cropped to 9:16.
Entertainment-heavy Shorts should normally include 4-6 meme/reaction moments, with visible image/video reactions preferred over an audio-only meme mix.
The first five seconds need a concrete hook, relevant real media, motion, and a strong editorial turn.
Never crop the foreground copy of a source image; only the blurred atmospheric background may use cover.
When a long entertainment-heavy Short has too few visible reactions, backfill unused joke, punchline, reaction, callback or analogy beats with approved image/video meme overlays.
Duck narration under audible meme overlays so reaction audio reads as punctuation instead of competing with the voice.

Pacing should feel compressed and editorial: remove dead air, keep narration roughly 180-195 effective WPM when natural, and reserve the fastest visual punctuation for jokes, reactions, analogies, punchlines and callbacks.
Do not merge humor/reaction beats into neighboring visual windows; they should normally receive their own visual punctuation.
Run discovery every 12 hours rather than using fixed posting time blocks.
Search all four discovery lanes on every scan—Major News, Market / Business, Hot / Emerging, and Creator Radar—but never lower the quality threshold to satisfy lane diversity.
There is no fixed daily story cap: zero, one, or many independently qualifying topics may be produced from a scan.
A single creator roundup may yield multiple Shorts when its topics independently qualify; decompose topics before scoring.
Creator Radar is a discovery, heat, context and explanation signal only; creator claims must be verified against primary sources before publication.
Merge the same development across lanes into one candidate and use convergence as a heat signal rather than publishing duplicates.
For Hot / Emerging stories, recent momentum can make an older project fresh; repository creation date is not the only freshness signal.
Do not clone or imitate the literal voice of a creator; use original narration with high-density, conversational, dry technical delivery.
Scheduled editorial batches must independently verify every accepted candidate with at least one primary source before a story is queued.
Heat and creator/community convergence may increase priority but cannot rescue an unverified or substantively weak story.
A discovery scan may queue zero, one, or many independently qualifying Shorts; there is no fixed per-day publishing quota.
Reach the target narration cadence primarily by native TTS speed and script density; post-tempo correction must stay subtle.
Use the scheduled ChatGPT automation as the sole autonomous editorial reasoning layer; GitHub Actions handles discovery, rendering and publishing without an LLM API key.
Editorial acceptance writes queue files only; history/covered.json is updated exclusively from successful render receipts.
Every qualifying topic must pass the multi-pass narration workflow in editorial/script-review.md before visuals are planned or a queue file is written.
The scheduled editorial worker must separate writer, critic/editor, rewriter, factual re-check and production-planning stages instead of treating the first draft as final.
A narration draft may proceed only when its script-review average is at least 8.0/10, no review dimension is below 7.0/10, and factual discipline is at least 8.0/10.
If narration fails the script gate, rewrite and re-score it; after three failed iterations, reject the topic for that batch rather than queue weak copy.
After a narration passes the quality gate, re-check every material claim against primary sources before creating semantic beats or visuals.
Production narration must use continuous Kokoro synthesis for the full narration; visual/editorial beat boundaries must never force separate TTS calls.
Do not trim trailing audio from Kokoro narration segments; preserve natural final consonants, decay and model-generated sentence endings.
Editorial roles control visuals, meme intent and script structure, but production TTS pacing comes primarily from natural punctuation and one continuous performance.
Prefer a slightly slower complete spoken phrase over speeding synthesis enough to crush final consonants or natural sentence tails.

Mathematical discoveries, theorem/proof results, algorithmic theory breakthroughs, and cryptographic results may qualify when the result is genuinely new, independently verifiable, and explainable accurately in a short format.

Confirmed data breaches, credential/data leaks, ransomware, supply-chain compromises, zero-days, malware campaigns, and major cyberattacks may qualify; distinguish confirmed facts from attacker claims and speculation.

Market / Business stories must involve a concrete catalyst such as earnings/guidance, revenue or demand shifts, M&A, IPO/financing/valuation events, major capex, material contracts, restructuring, or another consequential business event involving an AI company, Big Tech firm, or major consulting firm.
A stock-price move alone is not enough for a Market / Business story; identify and verify the underlying catalyst and explain why it matters.

Market / Business coverage may include OpenAI, Anthropic, Alphabet/Google, Microsoft, Meta, Nvidia, Amazon, Apple, Oracle, IBM, AMD, Intel, Broadcom, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Palantir, Accenture, Deloitte, PwC, EY, KPMG, McKinsey, BCG, Bain, Capgemini, Cognizant, Infosys, TCS, and comparable major AI/technology/consulting firms.

For private-company valuations or financing, use primary filings/announcements where available and otherwise require strong corroboration from high-quality financial reporting; do not present reported negotiations as completed transactions.

For Market / Business stories without a public primary source, require either two independent high-quality financial sources or one top-tier source such as Reuters, Bloomberg, Financial Times or The Wall Street Journal with direct sourcing/attribution; clearly label the event as reported, planned, discussed or under negotiation rather than completed.
Every newly queued production story must follow editorial/youtube-metadata.md and set publish.metadataVersion = 1.
YouTube metadata must be generated only after the final narration passes factual re-check.

New production metadata must include an accurate 20-100 character YouTube title, a concise description, 4-15 focused metadata tags, 3-5 visible hashtags, privacyStatus=public, madeForKids=false, and compact metadata-review scores.
Metadata must score at least 8.0/10 overall with no metadata-review dimension below 7.0 before a story is queued.
Do not put hashtags in YouTube titles, keyword-stuff descriptions, use irrelevant trending tags, or promise something stronger than the verified story supports.
The YouTube uploader appends missing primary-source URLs and visible hashtags to the final description automatically.
Metricool is a performance-feedback layer only; it must never delay uploads, lower editorial thresholds, or replace direct YouTube publishing.

If fewer than 5 Orbdev videos have usable Metricool per-video analytics, do not make performance-driven editorial changes; use 5-9 only as weak qualitative evidence and 10+ for soft repeated-pattern adjustments.

visualRules.preferredBeatSeconds: semantic only; not every beat is a cut
visualRules.preferredVisualHoldSeconds: 1.05-2.45 base holds; humor/reaction accents may be sub-second
visualRules.sourceImageTargetFraction: quality-driven, typically 0.35-0.55 when enough relevant official media exists
visualRules.visualWindowSelection: semantic relevance + editorial variety; explain is never allowed to dominate consecutive windows
visualRules.sourceCandidateMetadata: asset-local alt/title/context only; page title/description only for hero metadata
visualRules.explainWindowBudget: roughly 2-3 per 25-40s Short, depending on duration
visualRules.editingRhythm: meaning-driven base holds with sub-second meme/reaction accents; do not globally speed every scene
visualRules.firstFiveSecondsCutDensity: roughly 0.85-1.6s per major visual idea when readable

narration.processing: high-pass + very light compression + limiter + loudness normalization
narration.style: original high-density technical editorial voice: conversational, concise, dry/playful, clear explanation, varied sentence length and role-aware deadpan delivery; do not imitate or clone any named creator's literal voice
narration.speed: continuous Michael synthesis around ~1.34x base with conservative native retargeting; no role-based TTS chopping
narration.targetEffectiveWpm: 172 WPM center target; preferred natural band roughly 165-180 with complete consonants and sentence tails
narration.speechChunking: disabled for production narration; full narration is passed to Kokoro continuously and punctuation provides sentence-level prosody
narration.editorialRolesStillUsedFor: visual planning, meme intent, callbacks and beat semantics

preferredTopics: Big Tech earnings and AI capex
AI and Big Tech IPO developments
consulting firm AI revenue and demand
consulting firm acquisitions and material AI strategy

publishing.publishTiming: render/publish qualifying stories as soon as the scan/editorial pass completes; no fixed posting blocks
publishing.autoPublishTarget: YouTube direct via YouTube Data API
publishing.metricoolRole: analytics/performance feedback only; not publisher and not a scheduling gate

laneRules.major_news: major technical announcements and high-impact primary-source developments
laneRules.hot_emerging: GitHub, Hugging Face, Hacker News, open-source projects, developer tools, coding agents and fast-rising technical momentum
laneRules.creator_radar: topic-level discovery from configured creator channels; creator commentary is a lead/context signal, never ground truth
laneRules.market_business: material market/business developments involving AI companies, Big Tech and major consulting firms; require a concrete verified catalyst rather than generic price chatter

discovery.hotEmergingFreshness: use momentum age as well as creation/publication age

marketBusinessPrimarySourceException.evidence: two independent high-quality financial sources OR one top-tier source with direct sourcing/attribution
